newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Garanti Bank aims to grow by 25 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Turk Garanti Bank aims to grow by 25 pct in 1997.

text.p: Turkey's multi-branch Turkiye Garanti Bankasi A.S. targets a 25 percent growth rate in real terms this year, after reaching the same rate in 1996, a senior company official said.

"Total assets of Garanti Bankasi rose to $3.6 billion after a 25 percent growth in 1996 and we aim to grow at same rate amid expectations of favourable market and economic conditions," Akin Ongor, general manager of the bank, told Reuters.
He added that the bank's 1996 growth rate exceeded earlier projections.
Bank shares listed on the Istanbul Stock Exchange eased to 9,300 lira on Thursday from Wednesday's 9,500 lira close.

"We fully own Osmanli Bankasi in Turkey, United Garanti Bank International in the Netherlands and Garanti Bank Moscow and 85 percent of Bank Ekspress in Turkey," Ongor said, adding that the five banks' consolidated total assets stood at $5.2 billion.
Ongor is optimistic about the Turkish economy in 1997.
"The economy is not so vulnerable to political developments any more and is expected to grow by five to 5.5 percent with an annual inflation running at 70 percent levels," he said.
Garanti plans a series of moves to meet its 1997 growth target with the help of favourable market conditions.
"We primarily serve our customers as a bank instead of earning money by collecting deposits and investing them in Treasury bills and bonds," Ongor said.
Loans made up 52-53 percent of the bank's assets while state securities made up 13-14 percent in 1996.
Ongor said earnings from treasury operations, mainly bond trading existed, but the main income was generated from real banking activities like interests on loans and comissions from services.
Turkish banks made good profits from bond market operations in 1996, with real interest rates running as high as 40 percent.
Garanti Bankasi opened seven new branches last year and plans to set up 17 more in 1997 to increase the total number to 185, to attract more deposits and extend more loans.
It also plans to open 12 satellite-branches to provide teller services only for utility and telephone bill payments.
Ongor said automation investments in the bank's operational areas would continue this year to transfer a workforce of about 340 to marketing activities from back-office operations.
Turkish banks began to open more branches after the 1994 financial crisis to reach out to new customers as the major source for the system.
Before the crisis, the system relied heavily on foreign funds and hundreds of bank branches were shut down throughout the country.

Garanti Bankasi reported 329.6 trillion lira of total assets in the first nine months of 1996, against 131.9 trillion lira in the same period of 1995. Its net profits nearly doubled to 12.02 trillion lira from 6.14 trillion over the same period.
